tagline: A strategic capital allocator and expert risk selector in specialty insurance and reinsurance
hero_kpi_rationale: The Combined Ratio is the primary underlying performance indicator in specialty insurance, reflecting underwriting discipline and operational profitability. A ratio of 94.8% in 2025 demonstrates strong profitability with losses and expenses well below the breakeven threshold (100%).

kpis.name: Gross Premiums Written
kpis.explanation: Total amount of insurance premiums underwritten by the company during the year.
kpis.description: Gross premiums written reach $4.7 billion in 2025, up 7.1% from 2024 ($4.4 billion), driven by strong retention and targeted expansion.
kpis.signal: 7.1% year-on-year growth, supported by strong retention and new business opportunities.

kpis.name: Combined Ratio
kpis.explanation: Key profitability metric in insurance: sum of losses and expenses divided by earned premiums. A ratio below 100% indicates operational profitability.
kpis.description: The combined ratio stands at 94.8% in 2025 compared to 99.7% in 2024, reflecting strict underwriting discipline and the absence of significant adverse development.
kpis.signal: Strong underwriting performance with a 500 basis point improvement versus 2024, well below the breakeven threshold (100%).

kpis.name: Book Value Per Share Growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in diluted book value per share, a key indicator of shareholder value creation.
kpis.description: Diluted book value per share increases from $20.69 in 2024 to $24.61 in 2025, a 19.1% rise, reflecting value creation through capital management.
kpis.signal: 19.1% growth in diluted book value per share between 2024 and 2025, supported by profitability and active capital management.

kpis.name: Operating ROAE
kpis.explanation: Return on average equity, excluding non-recurring items and investment gains, measuring pure operating performance.
kpis.description: Operating ROAE stands at 8.5% in 2025 versus 5.6% in 2024, reflecting improvement in underlying profitability. The long-term target is set between 13% and 15%.
kpis.signal: Operating ROAE of 8.5% in 2025 vs 5.6% in 2024, demonstrating steady progress toward the long-term target of 13-15%.

kpis.name: Net Investment Return
kpis.explanation: Total return generated by the investment portfolio, including interest income and realized gains.
kpis.description: Net investment return reaches 4.4% in 2025 compared to 3.5% in 2024, supported by bond portfolio repositioning and a favorable interest rate environment.
kpis.signal: 4.4% return in 2025 vs 3.5% in 2024, reflecting favorable rate conditions and active portfolio management.

kpis.name: Book Value Per Share Growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in diluted book value per share, a key indicator of shareholder value creation.
kpis.description: Diluted book value per share increases from $20.69 in 2024 to $24.61 in 2025, demonstrating sustainable shareholder value creation.
kpis.signal: 19.1% growth in diluted book value per share between 2024 and 2025, supported by profitability and active capital management.

kpis.name: Combined Ratio Improvement
kpis.explanation: Significant improvement in underlying profitability driven by underwriting discipline and favorable reserve management.
kpis.description: The combined ratio stands at 94.8% in 2025 versus 99.7% in 2024, improved by underwriting discipline and favorable reserve development of $3.0 million.
kpis.signal: Combined ratio improves by 500 basis points versus 2024, reflecting operational excellence in underwriting.

risks.title: Volatility of underwriting losses and unpredictable catastrophic events
risks.score_rationale: Fundamental risk placed at the beginning of Item 1A with highly intense language ("volatile and unpredictable", "substantial losses"). Mentioned multiple times with concrete examples (Ukraine, Middle East, China-Taiwan). Trending upward due to climate change and increasing geopolitical tensions.

risks.title: Inadequacy of catastrophe models and modeling errors
risks.score_rationale: Major technical risk repeated four times in Item 1A with emphasis on structural limitations ("uncertainties", "incomplete", "inaccurate"). Specifically mentioned for wildfires and floods where modeling is less developed. Direct impact on pricing and reserves.

risks.title: Insufficiency of loss reserves and inaccurately estimated IBNR
risks.score_rationale: Critical operational risk with strong language ("no assurance", "significantly and negatively affect"). Specific to reinsurance with long delays between loss occurrence and reporting. Reliance on cedants' data, which may be delayed, incomplete, or inaccurate.

risks.title: Dependence on renewals and reinsurance market cycles
risks.score_rationale: Major commercial risk described across multiple paragraphs with details on market cycles (soft/hard market). Moderate language but material impact on premiums and results. Trend stable but uncertainty on the duration of the current hard market.

risks.title: Exhaustion of retrocession and unavailability of additional coverage
risks.score_rationale: Counterparty risk specific to reinsurance with strong language ("exhausted", "materially increase"). Mentioned with details on retrocession obligations, reinstatement terms, and credit risks of retrocessionaires. Trend stable but sensitive to catastrophic events.

risks.title: Unexpected accumulation of attritional losses
risks.score_rationale: Secondary operational risk distinct from major catastrophes. Moderate language ("may be adversely affected") but acknowledges that pricing models may not capture all loss sources. Trend stable but dependent on underwriting parameter effectiveness.

risks.title: Dependence on strategic underwriting partners (TFP)
risks.score_rationale: Specific operational risk mentioned multiple times ("strategic underwriting partners", "TFP"). Fidelis delegates reinsurance design and placement but retains final decision authority. Risk related to control and compliance with underwriting parameters. Trend stable but critical to operations.

risks.title: Sensitivity of the Insurance segment to economic and geopolitical conditions
risks.score_rationale: Sector-specific risk for the Insurance segment mentioned at the end of Item 1A. Moderate language but acknowledges vulnerability to global economic uncertainty. Concrete examples: credit, political risk, terrorism, cyber, mortgage insurance. Trend stable but sensitive to macroeconomic shocks.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence in the provided documents. The company does not position AI as a strategic or operational lever.
evidence: No reference to AI in the 10-K
No KPI or initiative related to AI mentioned
Exclusive focus on traditional underwriting, proprietary risk analytics, and capital management
